stories.title: 10-Year Treasury Yield Hits Highest Level in Nearly 20 Years
stories.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield has climbed to its highest level in almost two decades. CNBC traces the move to a mix of inflation expectations, deficit concerns, and shifting Fed policy bets. Rising long-term yields push up borrowing costs across the economy.
stories.whyItMatters: Higher long-term yields raise costs for mortgages, corporate debt, and government borrowing, and they pressure stock valuations.
whatToWatch: Upcoming inflation and jobs data that could shift rate expectations
Treasury auction results for signs of demand
Any Fed commentary on the long end of the curve
questions: What is the biggest driver: inflation fears, deficits, or Fed policy?
How long will yields stay this elevated?

stories.title: Muni Bond Yields Are in a 'Sweet Spot,' MarketWatch Says
stories.summary: MarketWatch reports that tax-free municipal bond yields have reached an attractive level for income investors. The piece frames the current rates as a limited window worth acting on. It comes as broader bond yields, including Treasurys, sit near multi-year highs.
stories.whyItMatters: Elevated muni yields matter to investors in high tax brackets looking for tax-advantaged income while rates are still high.
whatToWatch: Whether yields hold or slide if the Fed shifts course
Muni market demand ahead of tax season
questions: How long is this 'sweet spot' expected to last?
Are munis attractive after accounting for credit risk?

stories.title: Bitcoin Holds Near $84,000 as Rising Bond Yields Offset Regulatory Gains
stories.summary: Bitcoin is trading near $84,000, with Investing.com noting that rising bond yields are offsetting positive regulatory developments for crypto. The tug-of-war has kept the price roughly range-bound. Higher yields tend to pull money toward safer, income-paying assets and away from risk assets like crypto.
stories.whyItMatters: Bitcoin's sensitivity to bond yields shows how the broader rate environment is now a major swing factor for crypto prices, not just crypto-specific news.
whatToWatch: Whether Treasury yields keep climbing or ease
Further regulatory developments referenced by Investing.com
Whether $84,000 holds as a support level
questions: What specific regulatory progress is being offset?
Would a pause in yield gains be enough to push bitcoin higher?

stories.title: Charts: How Inflation Reshaped Prices Over the Past 5 Years
stories.summary: MarketWatch charts show how inflation has driven up everyday and big-ticket prices over the last five years, pointing to examples like $6 eggs and $50,000 cars. The piece uses these figures to illustrate the cumulative effect of price increases since 2021. It arrives as investors weigh whether inflation pressures are truly behind them.
stories.whyItMatters: The scale of price increases over five years is key context for Fed policy debates and for readers judging their own cost of living against market narratives.
whatToWatch: Upcoming CPI and PCE inflation reports
Fed commentary tying policy to these longer-term price trends
questions: Which categories have seen the steepest increases?
Has the pace of inflation meaningfully slowed from its peak?

stories.title: Apple Hit With $5.7 Billion Patent Verdict Over iPhone, Apple Watch Haptics
stories.summary: A jury has ordered Apple to pay $5.7 billion over patent infringement claims tied to haptic feedback technology in the iPhone and Apple Watch, according to CNBC. The verdict is one of the largest patent damage awards against the company in recent memory. Apple's next steps, including a likely appeal, were not detailed.
stories.whyItMatters: A verdict of this size could affect Apple's finances and its approach to licensing haptic technology, and it is a headline risk for the stock.
whatToWatch: Whether Apple appeals or seeks to reduce the award
Any statement from Apple on the ruling
Potential impact on future product design or licensing deals
questions: Will the verdict survive appeal or be reduced?
Does this affect other companies using similar haptic technology?

stories.title: US and China Agree to $30 Billion Tariff Cut, Launch AI Dialogue
stories.summary: The US and China have agreed to a $30 billion tariff cut and launched a new dialogue on artificial intelligence, according to Investing.com. The move signals a step toward easing trade tensions between the two countries. It also opens a formal channel for talks on AI policy between the two governments.
stories.whyItMatters: A tariff cut of this size could lower costs for businesses and consumers tied to US-China trade, while easing a source of market uncertainty.
whatToWatch: Implementation timeline and which goods are covered
Outcomes from the new AI dialogue
Market reaction in sectors exposed to US-China trade
questions: Which specific goods or sectors benefit from the tariff cut?
What will the AI dialogue actually cover or produce?

stories.title: She Grosses $300,000 From Pet-Sitting and Pays Herself $50,000. Is That the Right Split?
stories.summary: A MarketWatch reader asks about a friend who grosses $300,000 a year from a pet-sitting business but pays herself just $50,000 in salary. The column examines whether that owner-pay split makes sense for a small service business. It weighs reinvestment and business costs against personal income.
stories.whyItMatters: The question speaks to small-business owners and side-hustle operators trying to figure out how much of their revenue to pay themselves versus reinvest.
questions: What counts as a reasonable owner salary for a business like this?
How much of the $300,000 gross goes to costs before profit?

stories.title: They Earned $30,000 a Year as a Pastor and Still Retired Comfortably
stories.summary: MarketWatch profiles a person who earned just $30,000 a year as a pastor but still retired comfortably by living within their means. The piece frames disciplined saving and spending as the key to their outcome. It challenges the assumption that a high salary is required for a secure retirement.
stories.whyItMatters: The story offers a real-world counterpoint for readers worried that today's high rates and living costs make comfortable retirement out of reach on a modest income.

stories.title: White House Moves to Block $810 Million in Funding via Pocket Rescission
stories.summary: The White House is using a pocket rescission to block $810 million in previously approved federal funding, according to CNBC. The maneuver lets the administration withhold funds without a full congressional vote before they expire. The report does not specify which programs are affected.
stories.whyItMatters: The move raises questions about executive control over federal spending and could set a precedent for how future funding fights play out.
whatToWatch: Which programs or agencies lose funding
Any legal or congressional challenge to the rescission
Whether this tactic is used again for other funds
questions: Which specific programs are being defunded?
Will Congress or courts push back on the pocket rescission?
